chunks: There was a sign for the people of Saba in their habitations: Two gardens, on the right and left. (And they were told:) "Eat of what your Lord has given you and be thankful. Fair is your land, and forgiving your Lord."

key_terms.جَنَّتَانِ: Two gardens, referring to their agricultural abundance
key_terms.سَبَإٍ: The people of Saba, an ancient Arab tribe

ai.seo_question: What was the sign for the people of Saba mentioned in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to illustrate the principle of divine grace preceding human obligation, where the 'two gardens' symbolize both material abundance and spiritual potential. The command to 'eat and be grateful' underscores the Shia emphasis on recognizing God's mercy as the foundation for worship, linking physical sustenance to spiritual awareness of the 'Forgiving Lord.'
